notes:
Account snapshot: Aurora building an AI-first customer support product that will route and summarize multi-message conversations, surface knowledge-base articles, and run reranking for suggested responses. They are enterprise-focused (SAML + strict residency needs) and want a predictable dedicated offering rather than fully hosted for first rollout.

From AE/SE calls: shorthand notes and asks —
- Primary ask: guaranteed throughput + latency SLOs for production (p95 latency guarantees, per-route throughput targets).
- Target workload: real-time chat + asynchronous summarization + nightly bulk rerank. Mix of short (single-turn) and long-context (32k) sessions.
- Performance goals quoted by customer: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for short-turn 256-token responses; p95 <= 800ms for 32k-context summarization tasks (batchable). Throughput target: sustain ~800 concurrent chat sessions with 40-80 tok/sec/user average; peak bursts to 1.5k sessions.
- Cost sensitivity: wants cost per 1M tokens within 15% of current internal infra spend; willing to commit to reserved capacity if SLA compensates for outages.

Model & tuning items discussed —
- Models in scope: 13B and 70B LLaMA-3-style variants and a custom fine-tuned 30B for KB-grounded replies. Planning to test quantized variants (q8_0, q4_0, int8 where supported).
- Context length: 32k is must-have for conversation history + KB context; 64k flagged as future. Need clear perf delta table by context length.
- Quantization profile selection: prefer q4_0 for 70B to save memory; SE asked for side-by-side quality/latency comparisons (q8_0 vs q4_0) and deterministic fallback to fp16 for high-quality routes.
- Batching and KV cache: plan to enable continuous KV caching for repeat users, aggressive prefix caching for KB snippets. Target adaptive batching that respects latency SLOs (no tail-latency inflation). Suggested batch windows: 8-15ms for short chat, 30-50ms for rerank jobs.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial estimate 6-8 H100-equivalent GPUs for baseline; 10-12 for 2x headroom during peak. They want a clear mapping: concurrency -> GPUs -> expected p95 latencies.

Procurement & SLA negotiation notes —
- Customer demands: SLA with uptime, p95 latency credits, and guaranteed scaling behavior during release windows. Procurement wants 6-month ramp with opt-out.
- Legal flagged data residency and KMS entanglement for private control plane. Security asked for architecture diagram and KMS workflow (see linked drive doc).

- 2026-01-15: Intro call (AE/SE) — confirmed use-case and high-level constraints.
- 2026-02-03: SE deep-dive — discussed quantization tradeoffs and batching strategies. Action: Redwood to propose GPU sizing matrix.

- 2026-02-25: Security sync — provided SOC2 artifacts; customer requested KMS architecture + pen-test window.
- 2026-03-01: Cost/commit call — procurement requested ARR bands and optional burst pricing.

Open action items (short):
- SE: deliver per-model benchmark matrix (13B/30B/70B) at 256/2k/32k contexts with q8/q4/fp16 profiles. Due: 2026-03-12.
- AE: draft SLA with p95 latency tiers and credit policy. Due: 2026-03-19.
- Security: provide KMS integration diagram + HSM options. Due: 2026-03-10.

use_case_summary: Real-time chat for support with long-history summarization and nightly reranking. Requires deterministic quality on critical routes, low tail latency, and data residency for EU/NA customers.
requirements_summary:
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 200ms (short chat), p95 <= 800ms (32k summarization).
- Throughput: sustain 800 concurrent chats; peak 1.5k.
- Models: 13B/30B/70B family; support quantized profiles and an fp16 fallback.
- Deploy: VPC/private control plane with customer KMS; option for on-prem pilot.
- Observability: token-level cost + p95/p99 latency dashboards, per-route tracing.
